meta_description_en: Readers' letters to Outlet (April 1992): Matthew Weedall discusses Quizzard, 2MB drives for SAM Coupe, and Outwrite spell checker, with replies from Brian Cavers.
meta_description_ru: Письма читателей в редакцию Outlet за апрель 1992 года: обсуждение игры Quizzard, дисководов SAM Coupe, текстового процессора Outwrite и ответы редакции.
body_en_plain:
M O R E   M A I L ! !


    April, 1992      Page Reply


 How to write to us...02     -
 Matthew Weedall......03    07
 Mike Haine...........15    24
 Marc Broster.........27    31
 J. Kenrick...........34    36
 Reg Jeffs............39    40
 Jon Westgate.........44    48

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Matthew Weedall,

Ron and Brian,

First let me start by saying
thank you for running such a
marvellous 'Demo Compo' and
thanks even more for thinking
that I deserved to win. The
money will be put to good use!

Although I have no objection to
you altering any program sent in
by me I'd like to point out that
the modification to my Quizzard
program was incorrect. You see
the questions are not in the
form of true or false. If you've
ever played Domark's 'Trivial
Pursuits' then you will
recognise the type of input
selection that I had used.

The idea is that the contestants
read the question as it is being
displayed and when one thinks
they know the answer they press
his/her answer key.

The person then announces to the
other players what he/she thinks
the answer is.

They then press a key for the
answer to be displayed and if
they were correct they move the
pointer to the 'yes' icon and
select a ball on the board.

If they were wrong they select
'no' and the next question
appears. I apologise if I had
not made this clear in the
instructions.

It's a while since I have sent a
letter to you guys so here we go
with a couple of enquiries and
questions. I noticed something
about Coupe's being sent out
with 2 Meg drives - could you
please enlighten me on this?

I can remember when Coupe's were
sent out with no drive and 1/4
meg memory; I seem to remember
somebody saying they are now
sent with 1/2 meg.I know this is
simple progress and establishing
a computer on the market always
brings packages with it but I
can't help feeling resentful
about the fact that my system,
excluding the drive,cost me more
than the present systems with
twice the memory and a free
drive!

While on the subject of this, is
MasterDos/Basic being shipped
with them now?

I have a couple of questions Re:
OUTWRITE although I know that
you must be sick of people doing
so, but anyway, is there any
chance of a "Spell Checker"?

I can write a sufficiently fast
procedure but there is no way
that I am going to sit down for
a week and type in an entire
dictionary!

         Matthew Weedall

Brian Cavers to Matthew Weedall

Sorry about QUIZZARD! Now you've
explained it I can see clearly
how it should be played. I must
admit I've never played TRIVIAL
PURSUITS or I might have twigged
it. Anyway, we now have two
versions of the game working in
different ways according to pre-
ference! I suppose the lesson is
that programmers should think
carefully about instructions and
not assume any prior knowledge
by the user.

The two-meg drives are being put
in SAM Coupes because the manu-
facturer of the drives, Citizen,
has apparently stopped product-
ion of one-megs!

Apparently, it is cheaper for
them to have one production line
turning out two-meg drives than
two separate ones.

However,it is important to real-
ize that the two-meg drives only
operate as one-meg drives in the
SAM.You are not missing anything
- in fact I think they give more
trouble (I have heard that SAMCo
may go back to one-meg drives
from another source so perhaps
they have found more problems
also).

The only noticeable difference
in use is that the motor has a
more high-pitched sound. On a
one-meg drive, the head moves in
80 steps across the disc surface
from centre to circumference to


produce (in FORMAT) and read (in
LOAD) and write (in SAVE) each
of the 80 tracks that SAM uses
(on each side of the disc).

The two-meg drives are designed
to a higher tolerance with a
higher quality stepper motor
that can move in smaller steps
to give 160 tracks on each side
of the disc. Used as a one-meg
drive, as in SAM, the two-meg
drives simply make TWO steps
between tracks instead of one. I
doubt if even a special DOS
could format and use the 160
tracks the drives are capable of
- my guess is that the disc
controller chips used in SAM
would not be able to handle the
extra tracks. Someone tell me I
am wrong!

Regarding the decreasing cost of
hardware and the sense of
injustice felt by those who paid
the original higher price - this
is inevitable I feel. I bought a
16K Spectrum just 3 days before
the price of the 48K fell from
about `170-`180 down to around
`120 - about the price of the
16K when I bought it! I didn't
feel any injustice towards
Sinclair though - I just felt it
was bad luck! After all, I had
not lost anything - I had paid
the price I had been willing to
pay. The manufacturers are bound
to set a higher price at launch
and bring the price down when
they have recouped some of the
development costs and increased
efficiency(and thereby decreased
the cost) of production.

In fact, we should all rejoice
any time the price of SAM hard-
ware is reduced because it makes
it more competitive in the mark-
et place against the likes of
the Amiga and ST.

No,MasterDos and MasterBasic are
not included with SAM Coupe's. I
dearly wish they were!I still do
not use either as standard on a
regular daily basis because I'm
afraid of spending a lot of time
programming something only to
find it doesn't work on a normal
SAM! I have to write for the SAM
Coupe itself -not a non-standard
piece of software. There are
exceptions of course and I use
MDos/Basic as needed. OUTLET is
tested with all systems but is
only guaranteed on a normal SAM!

Nobody would be happier than I
if SAMCo bought the rights to
Mdos/Basic off Andy Wright and
included it as the standard SAM
DOS and BASIC. In fact here, I
DO feel a sense of injustice...
SAMDOS is sub-standard and a DOS
of the quality of Masterdos
ought to have been the upgrade
version. It's not so much the
cost of Masterdos/Basic as the
fact they are copyright.Users do
not appreciate this. They think
they can treat them like SAMDOS.
They can't (or shouldn't)! One
must restrict Masterdos/Basic
for ones own private use - not
share them with others. Programs
needing them can't be used by
anyone who has not got MD and/or
MB already and must not be inc-
luded on the disc!

However, I can understand the
market forces and appreciate how
difficult it would be for SAMCo
to afford to buy the rights to
MasterDos/Basic with no tangible
returns on the investment other
than (hopefully) improved sales
of SAM enhanced by the new DOS
and BASIC.

There is no chance of a spell-
checker being built in to the
code of OUTWRITE in the sense of
an advanced utility that would
test and challenge words as you
type - there is just no room and
it would be exceedingly diffic-
ult to patch in even more into
code which was never intended to
work that way.

However..

What MAY be possible is a separ-
ate, stand-alone program that
could load an OUTWRITE textfile
and test it for spelling errors.
It may even be possible to add
this option to the OUTWRITE menu
so that it would load such a
program while retaining a text-
file you are working on in mem-
ory, test the word at the cursor
and confirm O.K. or not - then
reload the OUTWRITE BASIC and
code in such a way that you go
straight back into the text at
the same cursor position. I have
never used a spellchecker to be
honest - only heard about their
different features. As you infer
- the greatest task would be
typing in the dictionary which
would have to be tested to be
absolutely 100% reliable! -Brian

      Mike Haine, Riverside
      Welsh Rd.  Offchurch,
      LEAMINGTON,  CV33 9AH

I wish more letter writers would
include their addresses. I so
often feel like writing to some
of you!

Re: Comments on my program and
article "KEYSET":-

I have just realised that I owe
Brian a profound apology. In my
remarks on the SAM keyboard I
quite forgot that Brian had an
earlier program and discussion
on the subject. I should have
made a reference to that, sorry,
Brian. (See OUTLET Issue 36,
"SHOKEYS").

I don't follow Alan Cox's remark
(Issue 53) about the manner of
changing the KEYWORD CODE. The
function DEF KEYCODE which I use
is meant for just that purpose
and does in fact do just what
Alan is suggesting. It redefines
the function associated with the
codes and pokes the mods into
the area of memory he suggests.

Since I wrote that, Issue 54 has
arrived (how time flies)!) I
won't comment on Alan's further
remarks, as he says, they say it
all again. There is just the
point that, for convenience, I
use the key LUT and SAM's most
useful 'INSTR' function to find
the keymap codes for the non
FUNCTION keys.

This assumes that those keys, in
unshifted mode,are left unchang-
ed. For the FUNCTION keys, how-
ever, it will often be desired
to redefine the key responses.
Therefore, I use a separate list
of keymap codes which I have put
at address &8990.

Ettrick Thompson says he would
like a listing of the keys and
their functions or Keywords. I
have now added this facility to
my program. From the menu, "L"
now calculates the response of
each key in alphabetical order
in normal, CAPS shift, sym.shift
and cntrl: The reponses are
printed to the screen in four
columns: The total occupies two
screens and the space key
toggles between them.

Once the list has been calculat-
ed it can be called from the
menu direct with "v".

Any further changes made
requires "L" again. While being
viewed, "d" dumps the screen and
RETURN returns to the KEYSET
mode.

I am sending the modified prog-
ram to OUTLET with this letter.

[In this issue as KEYSET 2 - BC]

I must say I find in writing
such programs I get very
frustrated because they are
never finished. No sooner have I
got one going when some fresh
idea or requirement crops up.

KEYSET could possibly be better
if it just used the alphabetic
key lists. Perhaps the keyword
list could be called up for
reference using the multiple
screen function.

That's the trouble. There are so
many super facilities on old SAM
that one has difficulty in
deciding just what to use.

Incidentally,I tried to use KEY-
SET with MDOS and MBASIC, mainly
to make use of the improved DUMP
facilities. It wouldn't run.

The reason is that lists in
memory are changed. This can be
corrected by use of SVARS...when
I have time.

READING and PRINTING OUTLET TEXT

For a long time I had a pad
alongside the computer and as I
scanned through the letters and
other items of OUTLET text I
made notes of items I wanted to
remember of take some action on.

The single page printing is use-
ful but takes up a lot of paper
space. I have written a short
piece of BASIC which can be
merged into the OUTLET BASIC and
which tells the printer to use
condensed mode, gives an input
query to set the left column (2
64 char lines can be printed in
condensed mode across an A4
sheet with spaces between).

If I don't want to print a page
but still want to print a note I
just press ESC to go into BASIC
and type in LPRINT "whatever..."
and use CNTRL x which gives
"RETURN" (key 263,182).

With other disc mags I load the
text items into Tasword 2 or
OUTWRITE. They can then be read
and edited, notes inserted,
unwanted bits deleted etc. using
the editing facilities of the
word processer. The relevant
bits can then be saved or
printed out using the 2 column
print out facility which I have
added to both word processers
and which printout the text in 2
64 char, columns. If you haven't
got these mods send disc & SAE.
[direct to Mike's address! BC]

It is not so easy to load the
OUTLET text items into the word
processors because it needs to
be decoded first. I have a
routine to do this but it needs
a bit of polishing. I will send
it in soon.

OUTWRITE. Re: Brian's comments
on my remarks in the last issue.
Yes, of course, one appreciates
most of those points but if no-
one puts forward what is meant
to be helpful criticism and
suggestions then how can we
expect progress?

Of course it is a commercial
project; but why should this
preclude acceptance of offered
help from outside enthusiasts?

(especially when they offer to
give it without charge?) Any
critical sounding comments I
make in no way imply that I have
anything but the greatest
admiration for the efforts of
RON and BRIAN in producing what
is undoubtedly the foremost disc
magazine.

           Mike Haine


Brian Cavers to Mike Haine

Thanks, Mike.

Regarding accepting help with a
commercial project, I would feel
rather uncomfortable about us
earning a living from a product
in which you had put some effort
and yet get no pay while we do
(because we cannot afford to pay
reasonable rates). It would also
have been extremely difficult to
keep you updated with details
and information of what we
wanted and co-ordinate efforts
of two separate programmers(both
with strong, conflicting views)
by mail. Were you willing to
write to order exactly our needs
or would you have wanted to put
in your own ideas? Ahah!)

Remember, you didn't agree with
some of the present routines and
even said they were "wrong" just
because you preferred a differ-
ent method. Supposing we had
asked you to write a routine you
didn't agree with?Would you have
done it our way?Perhaps. Perhaps
not. You have strong views!

I repeat, your offer is very
much appreciated but it is hard
to see how we could fit you into
the work - particularly as it is
now so far advanced and going
well.

At the time of writing the new
code is finished bar further
testing and I am polishing the
BASIC. There is far more in this
new version than I expected!

You refer to a "piece of BASIC"
to print condensed mode.I copied
all the files from your disc but
I can find no trace of any BASIC
except the new KEYSET 2. Would
you mind sending it again please
Mike next time you write. I must
admit I am surprised you say the
single-page printout from OUTLET
"takes up a lot of paper space"!
A full page of OUTLET text takes
less than TWO INCHES of paper in
64 column mode as provided!

Regarding readers' addresses I
reckon many just don't think to
ask that their full address be
shown and I won't publish it
without permission!Incidentally,
readers should REPEAT a request
to show their full address EVERY
time they write if wanted! B.C.

          Marc Broster,
        11, Church Road,
     SAXILBY, Lincs. LN1 2HH

Dear Brian,

Thanks for the help from my
letter in Issue 54 - much
appreciated. Thanks also for
publishing my clock program. I
also had second thoughts about
dumping my code in the system
heap but I tested the program
with Issue 50 of OUTLET and it
worked fine.

I am 'ever-so-slightly' dis-
appointed that I didn't win the
demo comp.I can't moan, however,
apart from the vast sum of money
I received for my effort.

Writing 'Excel' made me much
more confident with machine code
which is important.The best way
of learning machine code is by
having a go at writing a lengthy
program.

I haven't seen Matthew's demo
but, by what you said in your
letter, I expect it's similar to
Zenith Graphics' Chocolate
Factory demo? I was under the
impression when designing
'Excel' that you were looking
for innovative graphics, and
good programming, and not a kind
of lengthy animation.

You said you would have liked my
demo better if I'd given it a
purpose such as calling it the


"Blakes 7 demo", and writing the
scroller about the series. I
could have done this and
replaced the matrix sprite with
a spinning"Blakes 7" Spaceship
but would there be any point?
Most people would hit reset
after saying "Coo! That's
clever"as they would with Excel.

You said you were also looking
for something different, more
creative. It would be nice to
create a vector city where you
could watch what happens while
'King Kong' demolishes all the
buildings but I don't have the
programming experience to put
that sort of thing together. So,
I ended up with a scroller that
went behind the landscape, and a
large, animated main graphic.

The idea behind a demo is the
easy part. It's the programming
that's tricky!

While I am on the subject of
demos - what about the ESI demo
on the newsdisk? 4000 sprites
using the rom routines my foot!
My bet is that the part of the
screen with the balls is stored
several times in memory, and
each copy is updated then dis-
played in turn. Each copy of the
screen would have the balls in a
slightly different position so
that when rotated they look like
they are moving. It's a really
good piece of code, but still it
qets reset within a minute.
          Best Wishes,

          Marc Broster.

Brian Cavers to Marc Broster
Firstly - remember you asked ME
for my opinion on the program. I
don't normally give a criticism
of readers' programs!

Secondly - the program is O.K. I
merely pointed out why it failed
to achieve greatness!

Thirdly - calling it the BLAKE'S
7 DEMO was only to illustrate
the fact that such demos are
better with a coherent theme. It
made no sense to me to have a
screen like Blake's 7 which had
no relevance whatsoever to the
demo! I would not prefer you to
make it the BLAKE'S 7 DEMO -just
the opposite! Get rid of the
BLAKE's 7 screen and get a pic-
ture more relevant to the demo.

For instance, a general country
scene or abstract pattern would
blend better because your demo
did not HAVE any theme. That is
why it looked most odd to have a
distinctive screen like Blake's
7 tagged on. Sorry, if you can't
understand this but what I am
describing is what composing art
is all about and it is likely
that you just don't have the
"art" in your soul - nobody can
teach you - either you see it or
you don't. Try asking your art
teacher or English teacher or
even music teacher. Great music
cannot be written by someone
with no ear for music simply
arranging some notes in a clever
pattern. In other words, you did
not think about the composition

- you just took some nice music,
a nice screen etc. and put them
together - like a brown tie on
a pink shirt. This is not your
"fault". I am not complaining! I
am merely explaining!

I think your comment that "the
idea behind the demo is the easy
part, it's the programming that
is tricky!" gives you away. The
opposite is true. The big soft-
ware house have loads of highly
competent programmers to put
together their games. What they
are crying out for is what money
cannot buy - ideas!!!!! It's the
great ideas that make fortunes.
Who can remember the bricklayers
who built St. Pauls? No, we just
remember Wren. Right?   - Brian

From: J. Kenrick, EASTLEIGH

Dear Brian,

Thank you for the trial disk I
bought for the +3. (Dec. 1991,
Issue No.52). I was a little
disappointed that I couldn't
break into the Carol play (O) or
the Silent Night (H). I just
wanted to add a Y to play them
on my keyboard through MIDI. The
Xmas tunes (5) was okay and
sounded quite good.

Now I have acquired a 256K SAM
Coupe but I only have the User
Manual which is poor on detail
so any help will be appreciated.
If you do a SAM disc which has
programs then that will teach me
how to use the machine.

The SAM User Manual gives a
Swansea phone number but that is
dead. Any ideas how I can obtain
a Technical Manual?

           Thank you,

           J. Kenrick


P.S. Who and where is SAMCo?

Brian Cavers to J. Kenrick

Ah but you CAN break into the
programs you mentioned. However,
because of the way the Spectrum
128K is designed,the top half of
memory is paged out in 128 BASIC
and our standard character set
with it! Therefore the listing
is there - but undecipherable
garbage! We normally have a
special line at 9900 in most
programs that avoids this but
you just happened to pick on one
or two from which the line had
been removed for some reason!

There are two solutions...

One is to break in and enter
(blindly): POKE 23607,60.

The other solution is to reset,
enter +3 BASIC, enter...
MERGE "CAROLS", wait (up to a
minute or so while the screen is
blank) and then the listing will
appear.

We never intentionally use any
methods to conceal our programs
and, in fact, are always willing
to help if there is any problem.
Our policy has always been to
have "open" programs so readers
can examine, learn, modify and
back up our programs to their
hearts' content.

SAMCo are a new company formed
to produce the SAM Coupe after
the original producers, MGT went
bankrupt.

The SAM Technical Manual may be
bought for `16.99 from SAMCo at
Lakeside, Phoenix Way, Swansea
Enterprise Park,Swansea SA7 9EH.

I agree the User Guide is rather
short of information and, of
course, it's not a programming
guide as such. This month's
SAMCLASS will help you a little
with SAM BASIC. I don't what
time I will have to do others or
do them regularly however.Please
shout if you want more! Demands
by readers are listened to! I
would also be grateful for any
reader(s) to contribute SAMCLASS
articles at any level - advanced
or beginners, BASIC or machine
code. They should not be too
lengthy though in my opinion.
                        - Brian

From: R.W. Jeffs, LONDON, SE.18

Dear Ron and Brian,

How can I send UDGs to a printer
from the SAM Coupe? I've tried
to do this, (honest I have),with
no success, so what happens when
one enters the LPRINT option, it
leaves a blank where the UDG
should be and then it prints out
the data numbers. It will print
the UDG on the screen but not
the printer.

If you can help, Brian, it will
be a help to me and other
readers.
           Yours sincerely,

              R.W. Jeffs

Brian Cavers to Reg Jeffs

When a computer sends a letter
of the alphabet like a capital A
to a printer it just sends one
value which represents the
letter. For example, the value
sent for a capital A is 65. When
just printing text in this way,
the printer has no knowledge of
the way a capital A is shaped on
the computer - it uses its own
capital A shape whenever it
received the value 65. Printers
have all the common letters and
number and punctuation stored up
inside but it has no information
about the shape of a UDG on the
SAM Coupe.To send special shapes
like UDG's you need to send the
shape data thus...

10 CLOSE #3: OPEN #3;"B" : REM
   this prepares the SAM to send
   special codes. Spectrum users
   should use their own syntax

20 LPRINT CHR$ 27;"K";CHR$ 8;
   CHR$ 0;:REM tell printer to
   expect 8 bytes of graphics

30 FOR N=UDG "A" TO UDG "A"+7

40 LPRINT CHR$ PEEK N;

50 NEXT N

Take care to include semi-colons
as shown (;). Spectrum users can
substitute USR for UDG.SAM users
should first use SHOWUDGS(OUTLET
41) then insert the capital A
using SHIFT+A (NOT by using the
CAPS key).

Anyone who hasn't got(or doesn't
want!) SHOWUDGS then substitute
CHR$ 144 for "A".

Now, if you have entered it O.K.
and run it you should find the
character is printed on one side
and is a mirror image of how it
is shown on screen. This is
because printers use the data in
a different way to the way PRINT
prints on screen. You therefore
need to either design special
UDGs which will print the way
you want them too or use a rout-
ine to rotate them and produce a
mirror-image. FONTWIST 3 (OUTLET
54)does this. It is intended for
downloadable fonts so is not
suitable but might be adapted.
Let me know if you want me to
try.

There is another program in the
Spectrum version of Issue 36
called UDGPRINT if anyone else
is interested which does print
UDGS and rotates them but it is
a "closed" program for selective
printing by pressing a key and
is not suitable for including in
your own programs unfortunately.

What might be useful is a rout-
ine to rotate anticlockwise and
mirror image any byte which may
work on SAM and/or Spectrum as
needed. The central routine from
FONTWIST might be ripped out. It
is a bit slow if a lot of text
mixed with UDGs is to be printed
though.
                         - Brian

From: Jon Westgate, GERMANY

Dear Ron and Brian,

Firstly my apologies that I have
used WordMaster to write this
text, but I have no other word
processor.

In the Feb. issue of OUTLET you
mentioned in an answer to Colin
Macdonald that many of the high-
res screens that are included in
OUTLET are ported across from
ST, Amiga or PC's.

Could you suggest what software
could be used to port eg. TIFF
or TGA files from PC's to SAM,
or must one write his own
conversion routine?

I am assuming I can actually get
the files from the PC to SAM
either by transferring via the
serial port, or by using a pack-
age such as the PC Suite from SD
Software. I see the main problem
in the conversion itself, with
the differing resolution and
number of colours. Any help or
suggestions would be greatly
appreciated.

In the same issue, in your reply
to Stuart Burton on the question
of transferring Spectrum micro-
drive programs to SAM, you
queried whether the Messenger
and Interface 1 clash. I have
done this many times with an
almost 100 percent success rate,
however it is IMPERATIVE to
observe the following:

Load the Spectrum program from
microdrive and then REMOVE the
microdrive cartridge before
going any further! Now load the
Messenger code into the SAM. At
this point you can press the
button on the Messenger. The
Spectrum screen will start to
flash and the MICRODRIVE WILL
START TO RUN! If a cartridge has
been left in the drive it will
be totally ERASED! Now you can
start the transfer by selecting
H from the SAM Messenger menu.

This method appears to work
successfully, however, I am not
sure what the long term effects
are on the Microdrive's whizzing
around with no cartridge loaded
while the transfer is taking
place.

To stop the Microdrive, reset
the Spectrum and type in CAT 1,
or switch off the power.

I hope this will be of some
help.

Keep up the excellent work and
my best wishes,

          Jon Westgate


Brian Gaff to John Westgate

Thank you for the Messenger
information, it should help a
lot of those who were dithering
about getting one. The spinning
drive should not damage itself.
I have had this situation many
times through faulty programm-
ing. Once back in Basic, typing
STOP usually stops it. I suspect
it occurs due to the Messenger
doing an OUT that happens to do
odd things to Interface one.

Getting onto your other point
about translating screens, this
is not that easy! I do not know
about TIFFs or TGAs, but I did
download a file describing GIF
format, and decided it was
beyond me!

It would no doubt be possible,
given enough detail on the
formats, but as these files tend

## Letterc2

M O R E   M A I L ! !

April, 1992      Page Reply

How to write to us...02     - Matthew Weedall......03    07 Mike Haine...........15    24 Marc Broster.........27    31 J. Kenrick...........34    36 Reg Jeffs............39    40 Jon Westgate.........44    48

PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE! Text is accepted in any form for OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files (say which),typed or handwritten letters. However, PLEASE send us a textfile if possible so your letter needn't be typed again! The easiest for us to edit are Tasword 2 files with the right margin set at 32 but a textfile in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be parts of your letter you do not wish published but we always use our discretion anyway. Letters may also be edited for clarity and length... Please ask if you welcome direct correspondence from other OUTLET readers and we will publish your full address.

From: Matthew Weedall,

Ron and Brian,

First let me start by saying thank you for running such a marvellous 'Demo Compo' and thanks even more for thinking that I deserved to win. The money will be put to good use!

Although I have no objection to you altering any program sent in by me I'd like to point out that the modification to my Quizzard program was incorrect. You see the questions are not in the form of true or false. If you've ever played Domark's 'Trivial Pursuits' then you will recognise the type of input selection that I had used.

The idea is that the contestants read the question as it is being displayed and when one thinks they know the answer they press his/her answer key.

The person then announces to the other players what he/she thinks the answer is.

They then press a key for the answer to be displayed and if they were correct they move the pointer to the 'yes' icon and select a ball on the board.

If they were wrong they select 'no' and the next question appears. I apologise if I had not made this clear in the instructions.

It's a while since I have sent a letter to you guys so here we go with a couple of enquiries and questions. I noticed something about Coupe's being sent out with 2 Meg drives - could you please enlighten me on this?

I can remember when Coupe's were sent out with no drive and 1/4 meg memory; I seem to remember somebody saying they are now sent with 1/2 meg.I know this is simple progress and establishing a computer on the market always brings packages with it but I can't help feeling resentful about the fact that my system, excluding the drive,cost me more than the present systems with twice the memory and a free drive!

While on the subject of this, is MasterDos/Basic being shipped with them now?

I have a couple of questions Re: OUTWRITE although I know that you must be sick of people doing so, but anyway, is there any chance of a "Spell Checker"?

I can write a sufficiently fast procedure but there is no way that I am going to sit down for a week and type in an entire dictionary!

Matthew Weedall

Brian Cavers to Matthew Weedall

Sorry about QUIZZARD! Now you've explained it I can see clearly how it should be played. I must admit I've never played TRIVIAL PURSUITS or I might have twigged it. Anyway, we now have two versions of the game working in different ways according to pre- ference! I suppose the lesson is that programmers should think carefully about instructions and not assume any prior knowledge by the user.

The two-meg drives are being put in SAM Coupes because the manu- facturer of the drives, Citizen, has apparently stopped product- ion of one-megs!

Apparently, it is cheaper for them to have one production line turning out two-meg drives than two separate ones.

However,it is important to real- ize that the two-meg drives only operate as one-meg drives in the SAM.You are not missing anything - in fact I think they give more trouble (I have heard that SAMCo may go back to one-meg drives from another source so perhaps they have found more problems also).

The only noticeable difference in use is that the motor has a more high-pitched sound. On a one-meg drive, the head moves in 80 steps across the disc surface from centre to circumference to

produce (in FORMAT) and read (in LOAD) and write (in SAVE) each of the 80 tracks that SAM uses (on each side of the disc).

The two-meg drives are designed to a higher tolerance with a higher quality stepper motor that can move in smaller steps to give 160 tracks on each side of the disc. Used as a one-meg drive, as in SAM, the two-meg drives simply make TWO steps between tracks instead of one. I doubt if even a special DOS could format and use the 160 tracks the drives are capable of - my guess is that the disc controller chips used in SAM would not be able to handle the extra tracks. Someone tell me I am wrong!

Regarding the decreasing cost of hardware and the sense of injustice felt by those who paid the original higher price - this is inevitable I feel. I bought a 16K Spectrum just 3 days before the price of the 48K fell from about `170-`180 down to around `120 - about the price of the 16K when I bought it! I didn't feel any injustice towards Sinclair though - I just felt it was bad luck! After all, I had not lost anything - I had paid the price I had been willing to pay. The manufacturers are bound to set a higher price at launch and bring the price down when they have recouped some of the development costs and increased efficiency(and thereby decreased the cost) of production.

In fact, we should all rejoice any time the price of SAM hard- ware is reduced because it makes it more competitive in the mark- et place against the likes of the Amiga and ST.

No,MasterDos and MasterBasic are not included with SAM Coupe's. I dearly wish they were!I still do not use either as standard on a regular daily basis because I'm afraid of spending a lot of time programming something only to find it doesn't work on a normal SAM! I have to write for the SAM Coupe itself -not a non-standard piece of software. There are exceptions of course and I use MDos/Basic as needed. OUTLET is tested with all systems but is only guaranteed on a normal SAM!

Nobody would be happier than I if SAMCo bought the rights to Mdos/Basic off Andy Wright and included it as the standard SAM DOS and BASIC. In fact here, I DO feel a sense of injustice... SAMDOS is sub-standard and a DOS of the quality of Masterdos ought to have been the upgrade version. It's not so much the cost of Masterdos/Basic as the fact they are copyright.Users do not appreciate this. They think they can treat them like SAMDOS. They can't (or shouldn't)! One must restrict Masterdos/Basic for ones own private use - not share them with others. Programs needing them can't be used by anyone who has not got MD and/or MB already and must not be inc- luded on the disc!

However, I can understand the market forces and appreciate how difficult it would be for SAMCo to afford to buy the rights to MasterDos/Basic with no tangible returns on the investment other than (hopefully) improved sales of SAM enhanced by the new DOS and BASIC.

There is no chance of a spell- checker being built in to the code of OUTWRITE in the sense of an advanced utility that would test and challenge words as you type - there is just no room and it would be exceedingly diffic- ult to patch in even more into code which was never intended to work that way.

However..

What MAY be possible is a separ- ate, stand-alone program that could load an OUTWRITE textfile and test it for spelling errors. It may even be possible to add this option to the OUTWRITE menu so that it would load such a program while retaining a text- file you are working on in mem- ory, test the word at the cursor and confirm O.K. or not - then reload the OUTWRITE BASIC and code in such a way that you go straight back into the text at the same cursor position. I have never used a spellchecker to be honest - only heard about their different features. As you infer - the greatest task would be typing in the dictionary which would have to be tested to be absolutely 100% reliable! -Brian

Mike Haine, Riverside Welsh Rd.  Offchurch, LEAMINGTON,  CV33 9AH

I wish more letter writers would include their addresses. I so often feel like writing to some of you!

Re: Comments on my program and article "KEYSET":-

I have just realised that I owe Brian a profound apology. In my remarks on the SAM keyboard I quite forgot that Brian had an earlier program and discussion on the subject. I should have made a reference to that, sorry, Brian. (See OUTLET Issue 36, "SHOKEYS").

I don't follow Alan Cox's remark (Issue 53) about the manner of changing the KEYWORD CODE. The function DEF KEYCODE which I use is meant for just that purpose and does in fact do just what Alan is suggesting. It redefines the function associated with the codes and pokes the mods into the area of memory he suggests.

Since I wrote that, Issue 54 has arrived (how time flies)!) I won't comment on Alan's further remarks, as he says, they say it all again. There is just the point that, for convenience, I use the key LUT and SAM's most useful 'INSTR' function to find the keymap codes for the non FUNCTION keys.

This assumes that those keys, in unshifted mode,are left unchang- ed. For the FUNCTION keys, how- ever, it will often be desired to redefine the key responses. Therefore, I use a separate list of keymap codes which I have put at address &8990.

Ettrick Thompson says he would like a listing of the keys and their functions or Keywords. I have now added this facility to my program. From the menu, "L" now calculates the response of each key in alphabetical order in normal, CAPS shift, sym.shift and cntrl: The reponses are printed to the screen in four columns: The total occupies two screens and the space key toggles between them.

Once the list has been calculat- ed it can be called from the menu direct with "v".

Any further changes made requires "L" again. While being viewed, "d" dumps the screen and RETURN returns to the KEYSET mode.

I am sending the modified prog- ram to OUTLET with this letter.

[In this issue as KEYSET 2 - BC]

I must say I find in writing such programs I get very frustrated because they are never finished. No sooner have I got one going when some fresh idea or requirement crops up.

KEYSET could possibly be better if it just used the alphabetic key lists. Perhaps the keyword list could be called up for reference using the multiple screen function.

That's the trouble. There are so many super facilities on old SAM that one has difficulty in deciding just what to use.

Incidentally,I tried to use KEY- SET with MDOS and MBASIC, mainly to make use of the improved DUMP facilities. It wouldn't run.

The reason is that lists in memory are changed. This can be corrected by use of SVARS...when I have time.

READING and PRINTING OUTLET TEXT

For a long time I had a pad alongside the computer and as I scanned through the letters and other items of OUTLET text I made notes of items I wanted to remember of take some action on.

The single page printing is use- ful but takes up a lot of paper space. I have written a short piece of BASIC which can be merged into the OUTLET BASIC and which tells the printer to use condensed mode, gives an input query to set the left column (2 64 char lines can be printed in condensed mode across an A4 sheet with spaces between).

If I don't want to print a page but still want to print a note I just press ESC to go into BASIC and type in LPRINT "whatever..." and use CNTRL x which gives "RETURN" (key 263,182).

With other disc mags I load the text items into Tasword 2 or OUTWRITE. They can then be read and edited, notes inserted, unwanted bits deleted etc. using the editing facilities of the word processer. The relevant bits can then be saved or printed out using the 2 column print out facility which I have added to both word processers and which printout the text in 2 64 char, columns. If you haven't got these mods send disc & SAE. [direct to Mike's address! BC]

It is not so easy to load the OUTLET text items into the word processors because it needs to be decoded first. I have a routine to do this but it needs a bit of polishing. I will send it in soon.

OUTWRITE. Re: Brian's comments on my remarks in the last issue. Yes, of course, one appreciates most of those points but if no- one puts forward what is meant to be helpful criticism and suggestions then how can we expect progress?

Of course it is a commercial project; but why should this preclude acceptance of offered help from outside enthusiasts?

(especially when they offer to give it without charge?) Any critical sounding comments I make in no way imply that I have anything but the greatest admiration for the efforts of RON and BRIAN in producing what is undoubtedly the foremost disc magazine.

Mike Haine

Brian Cavers to Mike Haine

Thanks, Mike.

Regarding accepting help with a commercial project, I would feel rather uncomfortable about us earning a living from a product in which you had put some effort and yet get no pay while we do (because we cannot afford to pay reasonable rates). It would also have been extremely difficult to keep you updated with details and information of what we wanted and co-ordinate efforts of two separate programmers(both with strong, conflicting views) by mail. Were you willing to write to order exactly our needs or would you have wanted to put in your own ideas? Ahah!)

Remember, you didn't agree with some of the present routines and even said they were "wrong" just because you preferred a differ- ent method. Supposing we had asked you to write a routine you didn't agree with?Would you have done it our way?Perhaps. Perhaps not. You have strong views!

I repeat, your offer is very much appreciated but it is hard to see how we could fit you into the work - particularly as it is now so far advanced and going well.

At the time of writing the new code is finished bar further testing and I am polishing the BASIC. There is far more in this new version than I expected!

You refer to a "piece of BASIC" to print condensed mode.I copied all the files from your disc but I can find no trace of any BASIC except the new KEYSET 2. Would you mind sending it again please Mike next time you write. I must admit I am surprised you say the single-page printout from OUTLET "takes up a lot of paper space"! A full page of OUTLET text takes less than TWO INCHES of paper in 64 column mode as provided!

Regarding readers' addresses I reckon many just don't think to ask that their full address be shown and I won't publish it without permission!Incidentally, readers should REPEAT a request to show their full address EVERY time they write if wanted! B.C.

Marc Broster, 11, Church Road, SAXILBY, Lincs. LN1 2HH

Dear Brian,

Thanks for the help from my letter in Issue 54 - much appreciated. Thanks also for publishing my clock program. I also had second thoughts about dumping my code in the system heap but I tested the program with Issue 50 of OUTLET and it worked fine.

I am 'ever-so-slightly' dis- appointed that I didn't win the demo comp.I can't moan, however, apart from the vast sum of money I received for my effort.

Writing 'Excel' made me much more confident with machine code which is important.The best way of learning machine code is by having a go at writing a lengthy program.

I haven't seen Matthew's demo but, by what you said in your letter, I expect it's similar to Zenith Graphics' Chocolate Factory demo? I was under the impression when designing 'Excel' that you were looking for innovative graphics, and good programming, and not a kind of lengthy animation.

You said you would have liked my demo better if I'd given it a purpose such as calling it the

"Blakes 7 demo", and writing the scroller about the series. I could have done this and replaced the matrix sprite with a spinning"Blakes 7" Spaceship but would there be any point? Most people would hit reset after saying "Coo! That's clever"as they would with Excel.

You said you were also looking for something different, more creative. It would be nice to create a vector city where you could watch what happens while 'King Kong' demolishes all the buildings but I don't have the programming experience to put that sort of thing together. So, I ended up with a scroller that went behind the landscape, and a large, animated main graphic.

The idea behind a demo is the easy part. It's the programming that's tricky!

While I am on the subject of demos - what about the ESI demo on the newsdisk? 4000 sprites using the rom routines my foot! My bet is that the part of the screen with the balls is stored several times in memory, and each copy is updated then dis- played in turn. Each copy of the screen would have the balls in a slightly different position so that when rotated they look like they are moving. It's a really good piece of code, but still it qets reset within a minute. Best Wishes,

Marc Broster.

Brian Cavers to Marc Broster Firstly - remember you asked ME for my opinion on the program. I don't normally give a criticism of readers' programs!

Secondly - the program is O.K. I merely pointed out why it failed to achieve greatness!

Thirdly - calling it the BLAKE'S 7 DEMO was only to illustrate the fact that such demos are better with a coherent theme. It made no sense to me to have a screen like Blake's 7 which had no relevance whatsoever to the demo! I would not prefer you to make it the BLAKE'S 7 DEMO -just the opposite! Get rid of the BLAKE's 7 screen and get a pic- ture more relevant to the demo.

For instance, a general country scene or abstract pattern would blend better because your demo did not HAVE any theme. That is why it looked most odd to have a distinctive screen like Blake's 7 tagged on. Sorry, if you can't understand this but what I am describing is what composing art is all about and it is likely that you just don't have the "art" in your soul - nobody can teach you - either you see it or you don't. Try asking your art teacher or English teacher or even music teacher. Great music cannot be written by someone with no ear for music simply arranging some notes in a clever pattern. In other words, you did not think about the composition

- you just took some nice music, a nice screen etc. and put them together - like a brown tie on a pink shirt. This is not your "fault". I am not complaining! I am merely explaining!

I think your comment that "the idea behind the demo is the easy part, it's the programming that is tricky!" gives you away. The opposite is true. The big soft- ware house have loads of highly competent programmers to put together their games. What they are crying out for is what money cannot buy - ideas!!!!! It's the great ideas that make fortunes. Who can remember the bricklayers who built St. Pauls? No, we just remember Wren. Right?   - Brian

From: J. Kenrick, EASTLEIGH

Dear Brian,

Thank you for the trial disk I bought for the +3. (Dec. 1991, Issue No.52). I was a little disappointed that I couldn't break into the Carol play (O) or the Silent Night (H). I just wanted to add a Y to play them on my keyboard through MIDI. The Xmas tunes (5) was okay and sounded quite good.

Ah but you CAN break into the programs you mentioned. From: R.W. Jeffs, LONDON, SE.18

Dear Ron and Brian,

How can I send UDGs to a printer from the SAM Coupe? I've tried to do this, (honest I have),with no success, so what happens when one enters the LPRINT option, it leaves a blank where the UDG should be and then it prints out the data numbers. It will print the UDG on the screen but not the printer.

If you can help, Brian, it will be a help to me and other readers. Yours sincerely,

R.W. Jeffs

Brian Cavers to Reg Jeffs

When a computer sends a letter of the alphabet like a capital A to a printer it just sends one value which represents the letter. For example, the value sent for a capital A is 65. When just printing text in this way, the printer has no knowledge of the way a capital A is shaped on the computer - it uses its own capital A shape whenever it received the value 65. Printers have all the common letters and number and punctuation stored up inside but it has no information about the shape of a UDG on the SAM Coupe.To send special shapes like UDG's you need to send the shape data thus...

10 CLOSE #3: OPEN #3;"B" : REM this prepares the SAM to send special codes. Spectrum users should use their own syntax

20 LPRINT CHR$ 27;"K";CHR$ 8; CHR$ 0;:REM tell printer to expect 8 bytes of graphics

30 FOR N=UDG "A" TO UDG "A"+7

40 LPRINT CHR$ PEEK N;

50 NEXT N

Take care to include semi-colons as shown (;). Spectrum users can substitute USR for UDG.SAM users should first use SHOWUDGS(OUTLET 41) then insert the capital A using SHIFT+A (NOT by using the CAPS key).

Anyone who hasn't got(or doesn't want!) SHOWUDGS then substitute CHR$ 144 for "A".

Now, if you have entered it O.K. and run it you should find the character is printed on one side and is a mirror image of how it is shown on screen. This is because printers use the data in a different way to the way PRINT prints on screen. You therefore need to either design special UDGs which will print the way you want them too or use a rout- ine to rotate them and produce a mirror-image. FONTWIST 3 (OUTLET 54)does this. It is intended for downloadable fonts so is not suitable but might be adapted. Let me know if you want me to try.

There is another program in the Spectrum version of Issue 36 called UDGPRINT if anyone else is interested which does print UDGS and rotates them but it is a "closed" program for selective printing by pressing a key and is not suitable for including in your own programs unfortunately.

What might be useful is a rout- ine to rotate anticlockwise and mirror image any byte which may work on SAM and/or Spectrum as needed. The central routine from FONTWIST might be ripped out. It is a bit slow if a lot of text mixed with UDGs is to be printed though.


From: Jon Westgate, GERMANY

Dear Ron and Brian,

Firstly my apologies that I have used WordMaster to write this text, but I have no other word processor.

In the Feb. issue of OUTLET you mentioned in an answer to Colin Macdonald that many of the high- res screens that are included in OUTLET are ported across from ST, Amiga or PC's.

Load the Spectrum program from microdrive and then REMOVE the microdrive cartridge before going any further! Now load the Messenger code into the SAM. At this point you can press the button on the Messenger. The Spectrum screen will start to flash and the MICRODRIVE WILL START TO RUN! To stop the Microdrive, reset the Spectrum and type in CAT 1, or switch off the power.

I hope this will be of some help.

Jon Westgate

**От: Matthew Weedall**

Ron и Brian,

Сперва позвольте сказать спасибо за проведение такого чудесного «Demo Compo» и ещё большее спасибо за то, что посчитали меня достойным победы. Деньги пойдут в дело!

Хотя я совершенно не против того, чтобы вы вносили изменения в присланные мной программы, я хотел бы заметить, что модификация моей программы Quizzard была неверной. Видите ли, вопросы там не в формате «правда или ложь». Если вы когда-нибудь играли в «Trivial Pursuit» от Domark, то узнаете тип выбора ответа, который я использовал.

Идея в том, что участники читают вопрос по мере его появления на экране, и когда кто-то думает, что знает ответ, он нажимает свою клавишу ответа.

Затем этот человек объявляет остальным игрокам, какой, по его мнению, правильный ответ.

После этого они нажимают клавишу, чтобы отобразить правильный ответ, и если игрок был прав, они перемещают указатель на значок «yes» и выбирают шарик на поле.

Если они ошиблись, то выбирают «no», и появляется следующий вопрос. Прошу прощения, если не объяснил это достаточно четко в инструкции.

Когда компьютер отправляет на принтер букву алфавита, например заглавную A, он посылает лишь одно числовое значение, соответствующее этому символу. Например, для заглавной буквы A передается код 65. При обычной печати текста таким способом принтер понятия не имеет, как выглядит буква A на компьютере — он использует собственную встроенную форму буквы A каждый раз, когда получает код 65. В принтере уже зашиты все стандартные буквы, цифры и знаки препинания, но у него нет никакой информации о форме ваших UDG на SAM Coupe. Чтобы отправить специальные формы вроде UDG, вам необходимо передать данные самого символа следующим образом:

```text
10 CLOSE #3: OPEN #3;"B" : REM это подготавливает SAM к передаче спецкодов. Пользователи Spectrum должны использовать собственный синтаксис
20 LPRINT CHR$ 27;"K";CHR$ 8;CHR$ 0;:REM сообщаем принтеру, что нужно ожидать 8 байт графики
30 FOR N=UDG "A" TO UDG "A"+7
40 LPRINT CHR$ PEEK N;
50 NEXT N
```

Не забудьте расставить точки с запятой (;), как показано в примере. Пользователи Spectrum могут заменить `UDG` на `USR`. Пользователям SAM сначала следует запустить SHOWUDGS (OUTLET 41), а затем ввести заглавную букву A комбинацией клавиш SHIFT+A (НЕ через клавишу CAPS).

Тем, у кого нет программы SHOWUDGS (или кто не хочет ее использовать), следует заменить `"A"` на `CHR$ 144`.

Теперь, если вы ввели его правильно и запустили, вы обнаружите, что символ печатается одной стороной, и это зеркальное отражение того, как он показан на экране. Это происходит потому, что принтеры используют данные иначе, чем команда PRINT при выводе на экран. Поэтому вам нужно либо разработать специальные UDG, которые будут печататься так, как вы хотите, либо использовать подпрограмму для их поворота и создания зеркального отражения. FONTWIST 3 (из OUTLET 54) делает это. Она предназначена для загружаемых шрифтов, поэтому не совсем подходит, но ее можно адаптировать. Дайте знать, если хотите, чтобы я попробовал.

В версии для Spectrum из 36-го выпуска есть еще одна программа под названием UDGPRINT, если кому-то интересно, которая печатает UDG и поворачивает их, но, к сожалению, это «закрытая» программа для выборочной печати по нажатию клавиши, и она не подходит для включения в ваши собственные программы.

Что могло бы пригодиться, так это подпрограмма для поворота против часовой стрелки и зеркального отражения любого байта, которая могла бы работать на SAM и/или Spectrum по мере необходимости. Центральную подпрограмму из FONTWIST можно было бы вырезать. Правда, она работает медленно, если печатается много текста вперемешку с UDG.
